newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: COLOMBIAN SENATORS CALL FOR CONGRESS TO BE CLOSED.
newsitem.headline: COLOMBIAN SENATORS CALL FOR CONGRESS TO BE CLOSED.

text.p: Ruling party lawmakers have called on President Ernesto Samper to shut down Colombia's Congress and assume emergency powers to combat the growing threat of leftist rebels.

Others have demanded that Samper be impeached for his failure to rein in the escalating political violence from illegal armed groups of the left and right, who have pledged to disrupt coming local elections.

The contrasting calls, made by Liberal Party senators in a committee debate late on Tuesday, mirror comments made during the "narco-scandal" sparked by claims that Samper funded his 1994 election campaign with drug money.
Then some party members urged Samper's impeachment while others thought closing Congress would mute criticism they saw as distracting him from governing effectively.

"We offer to (allow Samper to) close Congress and ... make war or peace," Sen. Julio Cesar Guerra, a staunch supporter of the president, told reporters on Wednesday, repeating comments he made in Congress.
"We must do everything in our power to get peace in Colombia, even if that means shutting Congress and letting the president assume extraconstitutional powers," he added.

"There's no government here to protect us, and the moment has come to impeach (Samper) because he has lost his authority. Neither life nor honor nor anything else can be guaranteed in Colombia," Sen. Juan Guillermo Angel said in the debate.

In the last month, scores of civilians, mostly peasants, have been massacred by guerrillas and right-wing death squads across the country. At least five mayors were kidnapped by rebels in the southern province of Narino and released on Tuesday night after more than a week in captivity.

But the attack that most shocked the political establishment was the killing of Liberal Party senator Jorge Cristo, one of Samper's most loyal allies, by rebels of the National Liberation Army (ELN) in northeast Colombia Friday.
The rise in violence, despite Samper's calls for new peace talks with the country's Marxist guerrilla armies, comes ahead of elections for provincial governors and mayors set for October.
